evals.prompt: Our marketing site's LCP is 4.2s on mobile. The hero is a CSS background-image set by a React component after hydration, and we lazy-load all images. What should we change?
evals.expected_output: Identifies late discovery and lazy-loading as causes; moves the hero to an in server-rendered HTML with fetchpriority=high, width/height, srcset/sizes, AVIF/WebP, no loading=lazy; keeps lazy-loading for below-the-fold; states the 2.5s p75 threshold and recommends field measurement with attribution.
expectations: States the good LCP threshold as 2.5 s at p75 (not 2.0 s)
Recommends rendering the hero as an in the initial HTML instead of a JS-applied CSS background
Recommends fetchpriority="high" on the LCP image and removing loading="lazy" from it
Recommends responsive srcset/sizes and a modern format (AVIF or WebP)

evals.prompt: Add a dark mode toggle to our site. Users complain about a white flash when the page loads in dark mode.
evals.expected_output: Uses color-scheme meta and :root color-scheme, light-dark() tokens, an inline head script (or server-rendered attribute) that applies the saved override before paint, system preference by default, theme-color per scheme, and disabling transitions during swap.
expectations: Adds <meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark"> and sets color-scheme on :root or html (not body)
Applies a saved theme before first paint via an inline head script or server-side attribute, not in a framework effect
Defaults to the system preference and persists only an explicit override
Uses light-dark() or equivalent semantic tokens rather than inverting colors
Mentions disabling transitions during the theme swap

evals.prompt: Can I use scroll-driven animations and CSS anchor positioning in production for our dashboard tooltips and a reading progress bar? We need to support the latest two versions of Chrome, Safari, and Firefox.
evals.expected_output: Explains that scroll-driven animations are not in Firefox stable as of 2026-09 (progressive enhancement behind @supports), anchor positioning shipped in all engines by Firefox 147 but needs feature detection and a fallback position; gives @supports snippets and fallbacks.
expectations: States scroll-driven animations are not supported in Firefox stable and must be progressive enhancement
States anchor positioning shipped in all engines by early 2026 and recommends @supports (anchor-name: ...) detection or a fallback position
Provides a fallback that keeps the tooltip usable without the feature

evals.prompt: Should our new SaaS dashboard use Next.js server components or a client-side SPA with React Query?
evals.expected_output: Near-miss: rendering strategy and data fetching architecture belong to frontend-architecture. Routes there (optionally noting performance implications like JS budget), rather than producing a CSS/CWV checklist.
expectations: Routes the decision to frontend-architecture or treats it as an architecture question
Does not answer with a modern CSS Baseline table or metadata checklist
